newsitem.title: USA: Mother of obese dead girl charged with child abuse.
newsitem.headline: Mother of obese dead girl charged with child abuse.

text.p: Prosecutors said on Friday they had filed a felony child abuse charge against the mother of a 13-year-old girl who weighed 680 pounds (310 kg) and was living in filth before she died of heart failure.

Empty fast-food containers were littered about the apartment in El Cerrito, 20 miles (30 km) northeast of San Francisco, when police were called after Christina Corrigan's death last November 19, police Sgt. Scot Mosby said.
The girl's body was found with multiple sores amid feces and urine in a "dirty, disgusting" room, prosecutor Brian Baker said.
A medical examiner concluded the girl died of congestive heart failure due to morbid obesity, according to local newspaper reports.

Mosby said he was very surprised at the girl's obesity. "I've seen worse conditions in homes but I haven't seen a human who had achieved that much weight gain in such a short period of time," Mosby said.
The Contra Costa County District Attorney's office filed a felony child abuse charge on Thursday against the girl's mother, Marlene Corrigan, 47, Baker said. She is due to be arraigned on August 7.
After investigation, prosecutors filed the charge mainly because of the living conditions in which the girl was found, but also because her mother allowed her to get so fat, Baker said.
The charge carries a maximum sentence of six years in state prison, but prosecutors said the mother was more likely to get probation or a short jail term if convicted.

The Contra Costa Times reported on Friday that Christina Corrigan was found lying on a dirty brown carpet in the living room. The girl was 5 foot 3 inches (1.6 metre) tall and one of her thighs had a circumference of 54 inches (1.35 metres).
Her family told police the girl mainly lived on the living room floor in front of the television, the report said.
The newspaper quoted police as saying the mother did nothing to curb her daughter's weight since abandoning visits to a nutritionist when the girl was 7. The last time she saw a doctor was in 1992.
Marlene Corrigan told the newspaper her daughter tried "just about everything" to lose weight but nothing worked. In recent years, the girl refused to go to the doctor, she said.
Christina Corrigan, tired of being taunted about her weight, dropped out of school after 6th grade in June 1995, the report said.

Mosby said it was unclear if the girl had been able to leave the house. "There were no reports of her having been seen in the months preceding her death. Her mother said she did get out a little bit," he said.
Marlene Corrigan could not be reached for comment on Friday, but the Contra Costa Times quoted her as saying that she "should have done more."
"Every day I tell myself I should have done this, I should have done that. But what can I do now?" she said.
Corrigan told the newspaper she intended to plead no contest to the abuse charge, although she insisted she did not intentionally harm her child.
